subject: System Design
title: UDP: Speed Over Reliability
description: Learn UDP: Speed Over Reliability in one minute.

hook.text: In a video call, a dropped frame is better than a delayed one. UDP delivers fast — even if packets are lost.

buildup.text: UDP sends packets without establishing a connection, tracking order, or waiting for acknowledgments.

discovery.text: It's used for video streaming, gaming, and DNS — where speed matters more than perfect delivery.

twist.text: UDP has no congestion control. A badly behaved UDP sender can flood the network and overwhelm other traffic.

climax.text: TCP is reliable but slow. UDP is fast but lossy. The choice depends on what your application tolerates.

punchline.text: UDP trades reliability for speed — perfect for real-time apps.

quiz.question: Why is UDP used for video streaming?
options: A dropped frame is better than a delayed one
